editorial:
Ever felt like you were the only person in the room who didn't get the joke? That is exactly how you will feel meeting Mark. He is a guy who is just totally out of sync with the world around him. He cannot read a room to save his life, and he has zero sense of where his body is in space. The whole movie focuses on his hilarious and frustrating attempt to learn how to play frisbee. It sounds simple, but watching Mark struggle with a plastic disc is like watching a slow-motion car crash that you cannot stop laughing at. The vibe is light, awkward, and very relatable if you have ever felt like a fish out of water.

You will love the physical comedy here because the acting is spot on. The pacing stays quick, making the repeated failures feel like a funny loop rather than a drag. While the plot is very thin, the charm comes from Mark's stubbornness. If you want a quick laugh, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Mark finally manages to throw the frisbee in a straight line, but he does it by complete accident while tripping over his own feet. He does not actually learn the technique, but he catches a lucky break that makes his friends cheer. He realizes that he might never be a natural athlete, but he is okay with being the funny guy of the group. It ends with a big laugh as he immediately knocks over a cooler.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward humor and physical comedy.
